recipes.name: Lentil & Chard Soup
recipes.health: 22 g plant protein, 11 g fibre and 7 mg iron per bowl. The lemon helps your body absorb the iron. Source: AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines, guideline 6.
ingredients: 500 g Swiss chard (or spinach), chopped with the stems
recipes.method:
1. Rinse the lentils. Boil them in the water for 30 minutes, until almost soft.
2. Meanwhile cook the onions and garlic in the olive oil for about 10 minutes, until golden.
3. Add the onions, cumin and salt to the lentils.
4. Add the chard and simmer 20 minutes.
5. Stir in the lemon juice, simmer 5 minutes, taste, and serve hot.

recipes.name: Green Protein Smoothie
recipes.health: About 20 g protein, 6 g fibre, and more than a full day of vitamin K from the spinach. Greek yoghurt gives the protein, flax adds fibre and plant omega-3. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Put the water, yoghurt and spinach in the blender first, then the banana, flaxseed and ice.
2. Blend for 1 minute, until completely smooth.
3. Drink at once, or within 30 minutes.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats with Chia & Walnuts
recipes.health: About 31 g protein and 13 g fibre. Oat beta-glucan (about 2 g here) is the fibre that lowers LDL cholesterol; the US FDA accepts this claim at 3 g a day. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. In a jar, mix the oats, chia, milk, yoghurt and cinnamon.
2. Close the jar and leave it in the fridge overnight, at least 6 hours.
3. In the morning, stir. Add a splash of milk if it is too thick.
4. Top with the blueberries and walnuts. Eat cold.

recipes.name: Chicken & Quinoa Bowl
recipes.health: About 55 g protein and 6 g fibre per bowl, for muscle repair after training. Quinoa gives slow carbs and fibre; olive oil and lemon make the dressing. Source: AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Rinse the quinoa. Boil it in 250 ml water for 15 minutes, until the water is gone. Cover and rest 5 minutes.
2. Rub the chicken with half the oil, the cumin and half the salt.
3. Cook the chicken in a hot pan, 6 minutes each side, until no pink is left inside. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
4. Mix the lemon juice, garlic, the rest of the oil and salt for the dressing.
5. Put quinoa, spinach, cucumber and tomatoes in two bowls. Add the chicken and pour the dressing on top.

recipes.name: Baked Salmon with Lemon & Broccoli
recipes.health: About 34 g protein and 3 g omega-3 (EPA and DHA) per serving. The American Heart Association advises fish twice a week for a healthy heart. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 1 lemon (juice of half, the rest in slices)
recipes.method:
1. Heat the oven to 200°C.
2. Put the broccoli on a tray with half the oil, the garlic and a pinch of salt. Bake 10 minutes.
3. Push the broccoli aside. Add the salmon, skin down. Season with salt, pepper, the rest of the oil and the lemon juice. Lay the lemon slices on top.
4. Bake 12 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork. Serve at once.

recipes.name: Heart Nut & Seed Mix
recipes.health: A 36 g handful gives about 7 g protein and 3 g fibre. The US FDA allows the claim that 1.5 oz (42 g) of nuts a day, in a low-saturated-fat diet, may reduce heart disease risk. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Mix everything in a jar. No salt, no sugar.
2. Keep it closed in a cool, dry place.
3. One handful (about 36 g) a day. The jar lasts a week.

recipes.name: Blueberry Oat Shake
recipes.health: About 25 g protein and 8 g fibre. Oats bring beta-glucan, the fibre the US FDA links to lower cholesterol (3 g a day); this glass gives about half of that. Blueberries add vitamin C. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Put the milk, yoghurt and oats in the blender and leave 5 minutes so the oats soften.
2. Add the blueberries and cinnamon.
3. Blend for 1 minute, until smooth. Drink at once.

recipes.name: Foul Moudammas
recipes.health: About 20 g plant protein and 17 g fibre per serving, with iron and folate. Fava beans are a staple legume in the AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines for Lebanon. Their fibre slows the rise in blood sugar. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 400 g cooked fava beans (one tin, drained)
recipes.method:
1. Warm the fava beans in a small pan with a splash of their water for 5 minutes.
2. Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some beans whole.
3. Stir in the garlic, lemon juice, cumin and salt.
4. Serve in a bowl, topped with the tomato, parsley and the olive oil.

recipes.name: Chickpea Tabbouleh
recipes.health: About 17 g plant protein and 14 g fibre per serving. Parsley is very rich in vitamin K and vitamin C, chickpeas add protein and slow-release carbs, olive oil gives the heart-friendly fats. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central; legumes as in the AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines.
ingredients: 2 big bunches fresh parsley (about 120 g leaves), very finely chopped
40 g fine bulgur, soaked in water 15 minutes and drained
recipes.method:
1. Put the soaked, drained bulgur in a large bowl.
2. Add the parsley, tomatoes, spring onions and chickpeas.
3. Dress with the lemon juice, olive oil and salt. Mix well.
4. Leave 10 minutes so the bulgur takes the flavour, then serve.

recipes.name: Hummus with Veggie Sticks
recipes.health: About 8 g plant protein and 7 g fibre per serving. Chickpeas and sesame (tahini) give protein, fibre and unsaturated fats, and the raw vegetables add crunch for almost no calories. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt and water until completely smooth. Add a little more water if it is too thick.
2. Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with the olive oil.
3. Serve with the carrot and cucumber sticks. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Fish & Chickpea Tomato Bake
recipes.health: About 45 g protein and 12 g fibre per serving. White fish is lean protein and a source of vitamin B12 and selenium; the American Heart Association recommends fish at least twice a week. Chickpeas and tomatoes add fibre and lycopene. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 2 white fish fillets, 150 g each (cod or sea bream)
recipes.method:
1. Heat the oven to 200°C.
2. In a baking dish mix the onion, garlic, tomatoes, chickpeas, cumin, salt, pepper and 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
3. Bake 15 minutes.
4. Lay the fish on top, drizzle with the rest of the olive oil and bake 12–15 minutes more, until it flakes easily.
5. Scatter with parsley and serve with the lemon wedges.
